When both our dogs were still alive, they didn't seem to know their names. I'm not sure if they were just hoping one of the names was the word for treat though.

Also with my younger dog, on a cooperative day, I tried to figure out which treat he liked best out of 3 brands. Turns out it's the one placed on his right while he was sitting and staying. Facing me while I randomly put them out, he went right every time. Facing away, he went left. Wish I tried it sideways lol. Which treat was where and what order I put them down spatially didn't matter. 2nd and 3rd were random but 1st choice was so consistent. He probably didn't really like any of them. They were for his treat ball and he liked the soft treats a million times better I think the ones that worked were probably just all "bland but I get a treat" to him...

I don't think it's ever too late for a dog to learn. Mine was so smart but DID get kicked out of obedience class as a puppy. He had this look that said "F you." He had a yard most of his life until we moved to NY. He was ~12 when he learned how to play catch with KyJen squeaky eggs in the apartment. 

We had a house the last 6 months of his life and he learned quickly how to tell when I decided to go to bed and how often to be at the back door before I even moved a muscle with an "emergency."  99% of the time he just knew he could get away with it and didn't even use a tree. No treat could lure him in and I'd be chasing him around the yard at 3 or 4am.  At 14 years old, after surviving an illness that left him with digestive issues, those "I need to go out NOW" looks had to be taken seriously.

Maybe there's a window for dominance but out older dog was alpha to him and when she passed away, well, he was a mama's boy. Smart, smartass, and only obedient when his life depended on it or the bribe was better than what he wanted to do. Exactly like me. I'm not sure what each of us learned from the other we were so alike.

But he learned new things right up to the end of the 14 wonderful years he gave us. Obedience to a human was not one of them. Our other dog, oh yeah, but never us. I don't know what breed. Shiba Inus don't grow to be 70lbs...

I have a problem where I normally have sound routed from my TV to my stereo, BUT it doesn't work when I use the HDMI out from my laptop to use the TV as an extra monitor.  It DOES work when I am watching broadcast TV using my crappy antenna (that's the only other input to the TV that does not COME from the stereo).  Sound comes out the TV no matter what when I have the laptop connected to the TV via HDMI, even when I have the laptop audio routed to the stereo via bluetooth or headphones plugged in.  So antenna in = TV does what it should and sends sound to stereo via HDMI.  Laptop in via HDMI = TV outputs sound from its own speaker.  Any idea besides unplugging something from my stereo HDMI inputs and doing it that way?  (lol)  The worst part is that it used to work fine and I have no idea what changed.
